props.result:
# Flow / first version

## Goal
Help a small team identify today’s priorities and waiting replies inside one project.

## Core behaviors
- Create a titled task with optional ownership.
- Move work through To do, In progress and Ready.
- Mark and filter “Waiting for my reply.”
- Begin weekly review from completed work.

## Empty state
Start with three editable sample tasks and a clear add action.

## Acceptance
Changes appear immediately, remain while the page is open, and can be undone.

# Flow / 第一版

## 目标
让小团队在同一个项目里确认今日重点与待回复事项。

## 核心行为
- 新建任务时填写标题，可补充负责人。
- 看板分为待办、进行中与完成。
- 可标记“等待我回复”，支持单独筛选。
- 每周回顾从已完成任务开始整理。

## 空状态
提供三张可以直接修改的示例任务，并解释如何新增。

## 验收
修改任务后立即看到状态变化；当前页面内保留内容；撤销恢复上一步。

nodes.name: 阅读摘录与概念
nodes.text:
城市热岛：在特定条件下，城市区域比周边地区更暖。可以从地表材料、树冠覆盖、城市形态和人为排热理解。白天的地表温度不等于人体感受到的气温。单次测量不能代表整座城市或整个季节。

这是用于演示学习流程的整理材料，正式研究需要补充可核验文献。

en.name: Reading notes and concepts
en.text:
Urban heat islands describe urban areas being warmer than nearby surroundings under some conditions. Examine surface materials, tree cover, urban form and waste heat. Daytime surface temperature is not the same as experienced air temperature. A single measurement does not represent a whole city or season.

These are illustrative learning notes; formal research needs verifiable references.

nodes.name: 一组教学用观察

公园：树冠较多，午后体感较凉。

狭窄街道：局部有阴影，但通风受建筑影响。
夜间：硬质表面可能持续释放白天储存的热。
不根据这些描述计算温差或相关系数。

en.name: An illustrative observation set
en.text:
Illustrative observations, not actual measurements:
Park: more tree canopy, feels cooler in the afternoon.
Paved square: direct sun and a hot surface.
Narrow street: some shade, but buildings affect ventilation.
At night: hard surfaces may release stored daytime heat.
Do not calculate temperature gaps or correlations from these descriptions.

props.result:
## Day: how heat arrives
Sun reaches surfaces. Shade changes direct exposure; materials affect absorption and storage.

## Night: how heat leaves
Stored heat is released. Urban form and air movement continue to affect cooling.

## Keep the questions distinct
Hotter surfaces, warmer air and feeling hotter are related but not interchangeable.

## 白天：热怎样进来？
阳光到达表面；树荫改变直接照射，材料影响吸收与储存。

## 夜间：热怎样出去？
白天储存的热逐渐释放，建筑形态与空气流动继续影响降温。

## 一个提醒
“地表更热”“气温更高”“人感觉更热”是相关但不同的问题，不能直接替换。

props.result:
# Why does the shade feel different?

On one street, a shaded path and exposed paving may feel very different. Air temperature alone does not explain it: direct sunlight, stored surface heat and moving air all contribute.

During the day, tree canopy provides shade and evapotranspiration influences the heat environment. At night, surfaces can continue releasing the heat they stored.

Studying an urban heat island means recording time, place, surfaces and measurement methods. An average rarely describes the whole city.

*This is an explainer based on sample learning material, not a measured field study.*

# 为什么走到树荫下，会觉得不一样？

同一条街，树荫下和无遮阴的铺地，感觉可能很不同。它不只是“这里空气低几度”的问题：阳光是否直接照在身上、表面储存了多少热、风能不能穿过来，都在参与。

白天，树冠提供遮阴，也通过蒸腾影响热环境。到了夜里，白天晒热的表面还会慢慢放热。

因此，研究城市热岛要记录时间、地点、表面和测量方式。一个平均数，往往装不下整座城市。

*本文是基于示例材料的学习解释，不是一份实测研究报告。*

nodes.text: 故事名：灯塔来信。适合 8—12 岁读者。主角在退潮后的海滩捡到一封写给自己的旧信，落款却是“明天的你”。核心不是时间旅行的炫技，而是学会求助与照顾别人。三幕，每幕约 250 字，语言有画面但不故作深奥。

en.name: The premise
en.text: The Lighthouse Letters, for readers aged 8–12. A child finds an old letter on a beach, addressed to them and signed “you, tomorrow.” The story is about asking for help and caring for others, rather than time-travel mechanics. Three vivid, accessible acts, around 200 words each.

nodes.name: 阿澄与守灯人
nodes.text: 阿澄，11 岁，擅长观察，不愿承认自己害怕。奶奶过去是守灯人，现在视力不好。小狗栗子会叼走重要的东西，但也会把人带到正确的地方。阿澄需要从“独自证明自己”转向“和别人一起完成”。

en.name: The cast
en.text: Ari is eleven, observant, and reluctant to admit fear. Their grandmother used to keep the lighthouse and now has poor eyesight. Chestnut the dog steals important things but often leads people somewhere useful. Ari must move from proving themself alone to doing something together.

nodes.name: 海湾小镇的规则
nodes.text: 小镇只有一座旧灯塔，暴风雨前总会起雾。旧信不是预测所有未来，而是上一代守灯人留下的提醒：潮汐会带回人们没说出口的话。视觉：深蓝的海、暖橙色灯光、奶油色信纸；插画采用平面纸雕质感。

en.name: Rules of the bay
en.text: There is one old lighthouse. Fog arrives before storms. Letters do not predict every future; they preserve words people never said, carried back by the tide. Illustration direction: deep blue sea, warm amber light, cream paper and flat, layered shapes.

The tide had polished the beach. Beneath an empty shell, Ari found a letter with a salt-soft corner.

“Tomorrow, remember the light.”

Ari told no one. The lighthouse steps were longer than expected. Fog covered the white line along the path. Ari wanted to prove they were not afraid, but their voice shook when they called for Chestnut.

Three bell notes answered from far away—the rhythm Grandmother used to call them home.

退潮把海滩擦得很亮。阿澄在一只空贝壳下面发现了信，纸角像被海风啃过。

她把信塞进口袋，谁也没告诉。灯塔的石阶比想象中长，雾一层层叠上来，连脚下的白线也看不见了。她想证明自己不害怕，可喊出“小栗子”的时候，声音已经开始发抖。

Grandmother stood with the old lantern. Chestnut sat at her feet.

“Were you never afraid?” Ari asked.

“I was. That is how I learned that a light cannot be kept by one person.” She placed the key in Ari’s palm, warm as a small piece of sunset.

There was another line on the back of the letter: If you cannot see the way, call someone’s name. It was not a command to be brave. It was a marker left by someone who had once been afraid.

奶奶举着旧风灯，栗子蹲在她脚边。

“你以前不怕吗？”阿澄问。

“怕。所以我知道，灯不能只靠一个人守。”奶奶把钥匙放进她手心。铜钥匙暖暖的，像一小块被留住的夕阳。

When the light came on, three small lights answered from the sea.

Ari wrote a new letter: “Tomorrow, you do not have to do this alone.” They folded it into the box by the lighthouse.

At low tide the next morning, Chestnut brought back another empty shell. Ari smiled and waited for Grandmother.

## Act I · a letter in the tide

“Tomorrow, remember the light.”

Ari told no one. The lighthouse steps were longer than expected. Fog covered the white line along the path. Ari wanted to prove they were not afraid, but their voice shook when they called for Chestnut.
